title: Take Back Control of Your Mind
speaker: TED
sourceMedia: TED演讲｜念头不停内耗？学会夺回大脑的控制权_哔哩哔哩_bilibili.mp4
topicQuestions: What happens in the brain when we worry too much?｜过度思虑时大脑发生了什么？
How can you take back control of your attention?｜你会如何夺回注意力的控制权？
What helps you calm down when thoughts race?｜念头纷乱时，什么能让你平静？
source: 官方逐字稿 + Whisper 词级对齐

sentences.text: Thank you.
sentences.translation: 谢谢。

sentences.text: How many of your thoughts today helped you get toward your goals in life?
sentences.translation: 你今天有多少念头，是真正帮助你朝着人生目标前进的？

sentences.text: And how many of them hindered you?
sentences.translation: 又有多少念头在拖你的后腿？

sentences.text: Are you in control of what you think?
sentences.translation: 你真的能掌控自己脑子里在想什么吗？

sentences.text: As I first learned the answer to these questions, I was shocked.
sentences.translation: 我第一次找到这些问题的答案时，被深深震撼了。

sentences.text: I was staying at the Buddhist monastery Suan moch in the forests of Southern Thailand four years ago.
sentences.translation: 那时我正住在泰国南部森林里的一座佛寺——苏安莫克寺。四年前。

sentences.text: As you can imagine, life at the monastery is quite spartam You sleep on a wooden pillow and a straw stromat.
sentences.translation: 你可以想象，寺院里的生活相当清苦。你睡在木枕头和草席上，

sentences.text: You wake up at 4.30, meditate for 10 hours every day.
sentences.translation: 早上四点就要起床，然后每天打坐冥想十个小时。

sentences.text: Eat nothing but rice and vegetables and shower with a bucket.
sentences.translation: 只吃米饭和蔬菜，用一只水桶洗澡。某个特别的早晨，

sentences.text: One specific morning meditation session, I had a breakthrough moment.
sentences.translation: 在一次打坐中，我迎来了一个顿悟时刻。

sentences.text: It suddenly struck me just how little influence I had over the content of my mind.
sentences.translation: 我突然意识到，我对自己脑子里想什么，几乎毫无影响力。

sentences.text: I look back on my life ever since I was a child,
sentences.translation: 我回望自己从孩童起的人生，

sentences.text: And I could clearly see that my mind had always been constantly wondering distracted, unable to focus.
sentences.translation: 清楚地看到，我的心念一直都在不停地游荡、分神、无法专注，

sentences.text: And the reason why? Well, because I've lived the way I have, like any modern person, over-stimulated.
sentences.translation: 而原因在于——嗯，因为我一直像所有现代人那样生活，过度刺激。

sentences.text: It was my lifestyle that had produced this unsettled mind of mine, which had now become nearly impossible to control.
sentences.translation: 正是这种生活方式，制造了我这颗焦躁不安的心，如今它几乎已经无法控制。

sentences.text: For 20 years, I had been unable to recognize this phenomena within myself,
sentences.translation: 二十年来，我一直没能在自己身上察觉到这种现象，

sentences.text: Simply because my mind had never been provided enough space to observe its own functioning.
sentences.translation: 只因为我的心从未被给予足够安静的空间去观察它自身的运转。

sentences.text: There is a Swedish monk named Beyond lindeblod who lived as a Buddhist monk for 18 years before returning back home to ordinary life just a few years ago.
sentences.translation: 有一位瑞典籍的出家人，名叫比约恩·林德布洛德，他出家为僧整整十八年，几年前才还俗回到普通生活。

sentences.text: Upon his return, a journalist interviewed him and asked Beyond
sentences.translation: 他回国后，一位记者采访他，问道：“比约恩，

sentences.text: From 18 years as a monk with hours of meditation every single day, and no distractions.
sentences.translation: 出家十八年，每天打坐数小时、没有任何干扰，

sentences.text: What's the one key insight that you took with your home?
sentences.translation: 你带回家的最核心的一点感悟是什么？”他回答：

sentences.text: His answer? I no longer believe in everything I think.
sentences.translation: “我不再相信自己脑子里想的每一件事了。

sentences.text: It sounds so mundane, and yet it's not. And this, my friends, is why I'm here today, to introduce the radical concept that you are free to choose your own thoughts,
sentences.translation: ”这句话听起来如此平淡，却并非如此。而这，各位朋友，正是我今天来这里的原因——向大家介绍一个颠覆性的观念：你可以自由地选择自己的念头，

sentences.text: And thereby become an architect free to construct your own life by design.
sentences.translation: 从而成为自己人生的设计者，亲手打造属于自己的生活。

sentences.text: For some of you, this idea might be familiar. It lies at the core of most meditation techniques,
sentences.translation: 对你们中的一些人来说，这个想法可能并不陌生，它正是大多数冥想技法的核心；

sentences.text: Or perhaps it's a completely new one having yet to enter your mind. Or maybe, just maybe, you are now feeling that this is becoming a bit unscientific,
sentences.translation: 或许对另一些人而言，它是个全新的概念，还没进入过你的脑海。又或者，也许你现在觉得这有点不科学，

sentences.text: And you're silently wondering how an overdressed hippy got to the TED stage.
sentences.translation: 正暗自纳闷，一个穿着打扮过头的嬉皮士是怎么混上 TED 舞台的。

sentences.text: Well, regardless of your current standpoint, I humbly ask you to suspend any disbelief or belief
sentences.translation: 不管你此刻的立场如何，我都恳请你先放下一切相信或不相信，

sentences.text: Whether you are a corporate CEO or a surfer, I invite you to enter an open state of mind for the next 13 minutes.
sentences.translation: 无论你是企业高管，还是冲浪爱好者，我邀请你进入一种开放的心态，接下来的十三分钟。

sentences.text: Now, we find ourselves in a world where for the first time in history, more people die from eating too much than eating too little.
sentences.translation: 如今我们身处这样一个世界：有史以来第一次，死于吃得太多的人，超过了死于吃不饱的人；

sentences.text: More people commit suicide every year than are killed by war, criminals, and terrorists combined.
sentences.translation: 每年自杀身亡的人，比死于战争罪犯和恐怖分子之手的人加起来还多。

sentences.text: I wish to show you some data on our current health profile as a species.
sentences.translation: 我希望给大家看一些关于我们这一物种当下健康状况的数据。

sentences.text: This graph shows that as for today, percent of the US population are overweight.
sentences.translation: 这张图表显示，如今美国人口中有 75%超重；

sentences.text: For Sweden, that number is almost percent.
sentences.translation: 在瑞典，这个数字也接近 60%。

sentences.text: This one shows the 10-year increase in based medication being prescribed to children under the age of 17
sentences.translation: 这张显示的是过去十年间，被诊断为注意力缺陷、并因此服用安非他命类药物的17 岁以下儿童数量的增长。

sentences.text: For being labeled with deficit disorders.
sentences.translation: 被贴上了注意力缺陷障碍的标签。

sentences.text: And this one shows that as for today, nearly tenth of the Swedish population are now being prescribed anti-depressants.
sentences.translation: 而这张显示，如今近十分之一的瑞典人口正在服用抗抑郁药，

sentences.text: For US, that number is even higher.
sentences.translation: 在美国这个数字更高。不，

sentences.text: No these are some quite alarming data.
sentences.translation: 这些是相当令人震惊的数据。然而，

sentences.text: However, it could have been my personal data just a few years ago as I have experienced many of these states myself.
sentences.translation: 就在几年前，这也可以是我自己的数据，因为这些状态中的许多，我自己都亲身经历过。事情始于十年前，一连串可怕的事件，

sentences.text: It started 10 years ago now, and in a horrific series of events, my mother hastily died in an accident,
sentences.translation: 我的母亲在一场意外中突然去世，这毫无预兆，让我陷入一片混乱。

sentences.text: Which was unforeseen and left me in chaos. I was 14 at the time.
sentences.translation: 那时我只有十四岁。

sentences.text: A few years after that, I had developed addictions.
sentences.translation: 几年之后，我染上了各种瘾，

sentences.text: I had become addicted to cannabis, to sugar, to tobacco, to video games.
sentences.translation: 我沉迷于大麻、糖、烟草、电子游戏。

sentences.text: For some years, I lived a life where I was constantly distracting myself from the pain of the fact that the woman of my life had left me forever.
sentences.translation: 有几年，我过着一种不断用各种东西麻痹自己的生活，好让自己不去面对那个事实——我生命中最重要的女人，永远地离开了我。

sentences.text: In our culture, we are raced from the very beginning of our lives to crave stimulants, and the world we live in is an obvious reflection of this.
sentences.translation: 在我们的文化里，我们从一出生就被养成渴求刺激的习惯，而我们生活的这个世界，正是这种状态的鲜明写照。

sentences.text: And I'm not only talking about drugs, but think of anything we do, watching movies, watching sport events, eating cream cheese, listening to music, watching pornographics, going shopping.
sentences.translation: 我说的不只是毒品，想想我们做的任何事：看电影、看体育比赛、吃奶油奶酪、听音乐、看色情内容、逛街购物。

sentences.text: The list is endless, and all of these are consumer commodities. They are produced as a response to human need.
sentences.translation: 这份清单没有尽头，而所有这些都成了消费品，它们被生产出来，正是为了回应人类的需求。

sentences.text: We have lost control of how we used it.
sentences.translation: 我们已经失去了对自己如何使用它们的掌控，（那些东西）。

sentences.text: And have ultimately let them gain control over us and how we think.
sentences.translation: 最终反过来让它们掌控了我们，乃至我们的思考方式。

sentences.text: This was to the highest degree true for me and my past behavior.
sentences.translation: 这一点在我身上、在我过去的行为中，体现到了极致。

sentences.text: And whether you are a tech millionaire a Buddhist monk, a military officer, or a high school teacher,
sentences.translation: 无论你是科技界的百万富翁、出家的僧人、军官，还是一名中学老师，

sentences.text: You are, to some degree, being unwillingly dictated by your own thoughts, but also free to change that.
sentences.translation: 你在某种程度上，都在不情愿地被自己的念头支配着，但你也同样拥有改变这一切的自由。

sentences.text: The American psychologist and philosopher William James said that thoughts become perception.
sentences.translation: 美国心理学家兼哲学家威廉·詹姆斯说过：念头变成认知，

sentences.text: Perception becomes reality. alter your thoughts. alter your reality.
sentences.translation: 认知变成现实；改变你的念头，就改变了你的现实。

sentences.text: The world in which we live in, its quality, its character, is nothing but a reflection of our own minds.
sentences.translation: 我们所生活的这个世界，它的品质、它的样貌，不过是我们内心的投射。

sentences.text: And the only way to influence in which world you want to live in, or in which world you want your children to live in, is to learn how to influence your mind.
sentences.translation: 而唯一能决定你想生活在哪个世界、你想让你的孩子生活在哪个世界的办法，就是学会如何影响自己的内心。

sentences.text: I wish to share with you today what I have developed as the two most important methods on how to stop thoughts from controlling you, and ultimately take charge of your mind and thereby reality.
sentences.translation: 今天，我想和大家分享我总结出的两个最重要的方法，教你如何阻止念头控制你，并最终夺回对内心、进而对现实的主导权。

sentences.text: It's the realization that made me process the trauma of the death of my mother, the key insight from eighteen years as a monk by beyond lindeblod and the core idea from William James's statement.
sentences.translation: 正是这个领悟，帮助我消化了母亲去世带来的创伤——它来自比约恩·林德布洛德出家十八年的核心感悟，以及威廉·詹姆斯那句话的核心思想。

sentences.text: Method number one, practice meditation.
sentences.translation: 方法一：练习冥想。

sentences.text: Developing a habit of doing this for just fifteen minutes at a time, four days a week, can change your life. In many ways it did for me.
sentences.translation: 养成这样的习惯——每次只需十五分钟、每周四次，就能在很多方面改变你的生活，它就这样改变了我。

sentences.text: By definition it's the art of developing mindfulness.
sentences.translation: 按定义，它是一门培养正念的艺术，

sentences.text: It's practiced by consciously directing and maintaining your attention on an unstimulating object such as the breathing and doing this for lengths of time.
sentences.translation: 通过有意识地把注意力放在一个不带刺激的物体上，比如呼吸，并持续一段时间来练习。

sentences.text: This practice produces a more calm mind, less prone to overreaction, more rational and higher performing.
sentences.translation: 这种练习能造就一颗更平静、不易过度反应的心，更理性、表现更出色。

sentences.text: But the ultimate goal of meditation is to start objectively observe the mind. Let me give you a visual example of what I mean.
sentences.translation: 但冥想的终极目标，是开始客观地观察自己的内心。让我给你一个直观的例子，说明我所说的意思。

sentences.text: Imagine yourself a web made up of thoughts. Every thread, a possible thought path leading to different places.
sentences.translation: 想象你自己是一张由念头织成的网，每一根丝线都是一条可能的思路，通向不同的地方。

sentences.text: After some meditation training, one is able to identify thought patterns, see where they will lead, and choose to take another one.
sentences.translation: 经过一些冥想训练后，人就能辨认出各种思维模式，看清它们会通向哪里，然后选择另辟蹊径。

sentences.text: And this is what happened to me at the monastery.
sentences.translation: 而这正是我在寺院里发生的转变。

sentences.text: As I started to see which one of my thought path led me to anxiety and had done so for so many years, I was actually able to direct my thoughts towards something constructive instead.
sentences.translation: 当我开始看清自己的哪些思路把我带向焦虑，并且这么多年来一直如此时，我反而能够把思绪引向积极建设的方向。（而不是相反。）

sentences.text: And this means that as you gradually learn the structure of your own web of thoughts, you become able to actively predict which thought will lead to a which emotional state.
sentences.translation: 这就意味着，随着你逐渐看清自己这张念头之网的构造，你就能主动预判哪个念头会引发哪种情绪状态，

sentences.text: Which will make you able to actively choose states such as calmness, serenity and high focus over stress, anxiety and anger.
sentences.translation: 从而能够主动选择平静、安宁、高度专注，而不是压力、焦虑和愤怒。

sentences.text: In theory quite clear, but again, it can only happen as the mind is provided enough space and silence without being constantly stimulated.
sentences.translation: 理论上很清楚，但同样地，只有当内心被给予足够的空间和宁静、不被无休止地刺激时，这一切才会发生。

sentences.text: Method number two, restrain your mental and physical input. The saying that you are what you eat certainly applies to food.
sentences.translation: 方法二：节制你输入大脑的信息和身体的摄入。“你吃什么就是什么”这句话当然适用于食物，

sentences.text: But have you ever thought of the notion of bad information having the same effect, making us mentally unhealthy, obese, addicted?
sentences.translation: 但你有没有想过，坏信息也会产生同样的效果，让我们在精神上变得不健康、臃肿、上瘾？

sentences.text: In our age of information, an unprecedented junk data load enters our minds every single day. And this junk data then influences our minds.
sentences.translation: 在这个信息时代，前所未有的海量垃圾数据，每天都在涌入我们的大脑，而这些垃圾数据接着影响我们的内心，

sentences.text: It affects our values, it creates our needs and desires and even how we think.
sentences.translation: 左右我们的价值观，制造我们的需求和欲望，甚至改变我们的思维方式。

sentences.text: It's our responsibility as individuals to carefully feed our minds with selected input, and that input then, if chosen wisely, will produce this desirable mental environment in which we can start to understand our minds properly enough to control them.
sentences.translation: 作为个体，我们有责任谨慎地给内心喂食经过筛选的信息，而这些信息如果选择得当，就会营造出理想的心理环境，让我们能够充分地了解自己的内心，进而掌控它。

sentences.text: I want you to ask yourself, is it constructive for me to be bombarded daily with newspaper tablets of death, sex, fear and terrorists?
sentences.translation: 我想让你问问自己：每天被报纸上那些关于死亡、性、恐惧和恐怖分子的内容狂轰滥炸，对我真的有益吗？

sentences.text: In my mind, the majority of newspapers are more important for terrorists than terrorists themselves.
sentences.translation: 在我看来，大多数报纸对恐怖分子的意义，比恐怖分子本身还要大。

sentences.text: Choose your media source wisely because they are seldom designed only to transmit information.
sentences.translation: 请谨慎选择你的信息来源，因为它们很少只是为了传递信息而设计，

sentences.text: More often than not, their primary objective is to spark your interest using catchy headlines fueled with fear and sex, which happens on direct expense of fact.
sentences.translation: 更多时候，它们的首要目的是用那些充满恐惧和性暗示的、耸人听闻的标题，勾起你的兴趣，而这直接以牺牲事实为代价。

sentences.text: Social media, such a brilliant tool when used right and so catastrophic when abused, no stimulant has ever in a society so addicted, so immersed in such a short time.
sentences.translation: 社交媒体——用得对，它是一个绝妙的工具；用得不当，它则极具破坏力。没有任何一种兴奋剂，曾让一个社会在如此短的时间内，变得如此上瘾、如此深陷其中。

sentences.text: Did you know that the term Facebook addiction disorder has emerged as a valid disorder, causing witherable excessive use and term anxiety?
sentences.translation: 你知道吗，“脸书上瘾症”已经成为一种公认的病症，它会造成过度使用和长期的焦虑。

sentences.text: There is a recent study from the University of Pittsburgh, has now showed that the more we use social media, the more socially isolated we feel, and the more socially isolated we feel, the more we want to use social media.
sentences.translation: 匹兹堡大学最近的一项研究已经表明：我们使用社交媒体的时间越多，就越感到社交孤立；而越感到社交孤立，就越想使用社交媒体。所以，

sentences.text: So just like a drug, we feel that by getting a speed fixed injected to our minds, it will make us feel better, but it actually makes us feel worse.
sentences.translation: 就像毒品一样，我们觉得给大脑注入一剂新的“兴奋剂”会让我们感觉更好，但实际上它只会让我们感觉更糟。

sentences.text: So friends, you have to take control over your use of social media, otherwise social media will start to take control over you.
sentences.translation: 所以，朋友们，你必须掌控自己对社交媒体的使用，否则社交媒体就会开始反过来掌控你。

sentences.text: Advertisements are also sources of often polluted information, think for example of sugary unhealthy food products, quite a few commercials out there for them.
sentences.translation: 广告也是经常被污染的信息来源。想想那些高糖、不健康的食品产品，市面上有不少它们的广告。

sentences.text: And now sugar, the substance sugar, is our global number one health threat as a species, killing more people every year than heroine cocaine and amphetamine combined.
sentences.translation: 而糖——糖这个物质，是我们整个人类面临的全球头号健康威胁，它每年杀死的人比海洛因、可卡因和安非他命加起来还要多。

sentences.text: So what can we do? Stop sugar and based products from being sold and marketed?
sentences.translation: 那么我们能做什么呢？停止销售和营销糖以及含糖产品？当然不可能，

sentences.text: Of course not, because they are not inherently bad. Sugar is great for a lot of people, right? The problem does not lie in the externality.
sentences.translation: 因为它们本身并非坏东西。糖对很多人来说是很棒的东西，对吧。问题并不在外部世界。

sentences.text: We need to take responsibility over our thoughts and impulses when being exposed to when consuming these products and their commercials and realize that their incentive for your consumption is not to benefit you.
sentences.translation: 当我们面对这些产品及其广告时，我们需要对自己的念头和冲动负责，要意识到，他们诱导你消费，并不是为了你的利益。现在想想，

sentences.text: Now, think of this. The human operating system is designed through millions of years of evolution to reward the behavior that promotes survival in an environment of constant territorial threats and scarce resources.
sentences.translation: 人类这套“操作系统”，是经过数百万年的演化设计出来的，为的是奖励那些在充满领土威胁和稀缺资源的环境中能促进生存的行为。

sentences.text: In that world, eating as much honey as possible meant survival, so did killing other tribes when intruding on your territory.
sentences.translation: 在那个世界里，尽可能多地吃蜂蜜意味着生存；当别的部落入侵你的领地时，消灭他们也一样。

sentences.text: But man has come out of the jungle where there was not enough, and we built a whole ethic around not having enough.
sentences.translation: 但人类已经走出了那个物资匮乏的丛林，我们围绕“匮乏”建立了一整套伦理。随着环境的彻底改变，

sentences.text: As our environment has completely shifted, our mental operating system has gone dangerously obsolete.
sentences.translation: 我们的心理操作系统已经危险地过时了。

sentences.text: It's time for an upgrade. We need to transition from being smart monkeys and become conscious beings.
sentences.translation: 是时候了，我们需要完成一次转变，从聪明的猴子，进化成为有意识的生灵。

sentences.text: You are like me, a homo sapience wise human, member of the first known life form to develop consciousness.
sentences.translation: 你和我一样，是智人，是已知的第一种发展出意识的生命形态。

sentences.text: You are the pinnacle of evolution. Now please reflect upon the stories I've told, which are yours, and decide what you want to do with them.
sentences.translation: 你是进化的顶点。现在，请好好想想我讲的这些故事，哪些是你的，并决定你要如何对待它们。

sentences.text: Because friends, it's not the harsh, traumatic or horrible events themselves you should fear the most in life.
sentences.translation: 因为，朋友们，人生中最该让你恐惧的，并不是那些残酷、

sentences.text: But your own unwillingness to control your reaction to those events.
sentences.translation: 创伤或可怕的事件本身，而是你不愿意去掌控自己对这些事件的反应。

sentences.text: Ultimately, it's your capacity to take full responsibility for your thoughts that will dictate the course and growth of not just you, but our entire world.
sentences.translation: 归根结底，能否对自己的念头负起全部责任，将决定不只你个人的成长轨迹，还有我们整个世界的走向。

sentences.text: Thank you so much for letting me be part of this.
sentences.translation: 非常感谢，让我得以参与其中。

alignmentNote: 用户提供逐字稿的真实时间码 + 音素权重词级插值

clips.summary: 开场抛出三个问题：今天你的念头里，有多少在帮助你朝人生目标前进，又有多少在拖你后腿？你真的能掌控自己在想什么吗？讲者说，他第一次找到这些问题的答案时，被深深震撼了。

keyPoints.phrase: helped you get toward your goals in life
Are you in control of what you think

clips.summary: 四年前他住在泰国森林的苏安莫克寺，生活清苦：木枕草席、四点起床、每天打坐十小时。某天早晨打坐时他突然顿悟，意识到自己几乎无法掌控脑中内容；回望一生，他的心念一直在游荡、分神、无法专注，皆因过度刺激的现代生活方式。

synonyms: ten hours of meditation a day

keyPoints.phrase: how little influence I had over the content of my mind
synonyms: how little control I had over my thoughts
how little power over my mind

clips.summary: 瑞典僧人比约恩·林德布洛德出家十八年后还俗，被记者问到带回家的核心感悟，他答道：「我不再相信自己脑子里想的每一件事。」讲者由此引出核心理念：你可以自由选择自己的念头，成为人生的设计者。他恳请大家放下成见，以开放心态聆听。

keyPoints.phrase: I no longer believe in everything I think
synonyms: I don't believe every thought I have
I stopped trusting all my thoughts

keyPoints.phrase: free to choose your own thoughts
architect free to construct your own life

clips.summary: 如今有史以来第一次，死于吃太多的人超过死于吃不饱的人；每年自杀人数超过战争、罪犯与恐怖分子造成的死亡总和。图表显示美国 75% 人口超重，瑞典接近 60%；被诊断为注意力缺陷而服药的儿童激增，近十分之一瑞典人服用抗抑郁药——这些数据令人震惊。

keyPoints.phrase: more people die from eating too much than eating too little
synonyms: more die from overeating than starvation

clips.summary: 这些状态他自己也大多经历过：十年前母亲在一场意外中突然去世，当时他才十四岁；几年后他染上了大麻、糖、烟草和电子游戏的瘾，多年来不断麻痹自己，好逃避「生命中最重要的女人永远离开」的痛苦。

keyPoints.phrase: my mother hastily died in an accident
synonyms: my mother died suddenly in an accident
my mother died in an accident

keyPoints.phrase: the woman of my life had left me forever
synonyms: the most important woman left me forever
the love of my life was gone

clips.summary: 在我们的文化里，人从一出生就被养成渴求刺激，世界正是其写照。电影、体育、音乐、色情、购物……这些消费品反客为主，我们失去了对自己如何使用的掌控，最终让它们掌控了我们的思考。无论你是谁，都在某种程度上被念头支配，但也拥有改变的自由。
威廉·詹姆斯说：念头变成认知，认知变成现实；改变你的念头，就改变了你的现实。我们生活的世界只是内心的投射。因此，唯一能决定你想生活在哪个世界的办法，就是学会影响自己的内心。他今天要分享两大最重要的方法。
方法一：练习冥想。每次十五分钟、每周四次即可改变生活。冥想是培养正念的艺术，把注意力有意识地放在呼吸这类不带刺激的对象上。终极目标是客观观察内心——想象自己是一张念头织成的网，看清每条思路通向哪里，从而主动选择平静、安宁与专注。

keyPoints.phrase: a web made up of thoughts

clips.summary: 方法二：节制你输入大脑的信息和身体的摄入。「你吃什么就是什么」也适用于信息——坏信息同样让我们精神上不健康、臃肿、上瘾。信息时代每天有海量垃圾数据涌入大脑，作为个体，我们有责任谨慎地给内心喂食经过筛选的信息。

keyPoints.phrase: restrain your mental and physical input
synonyms: limit your mental and physical input

clips.summary: 问问自己：每天被报纸上死亡、性、恐惧、恐怖分子的内容轰炸，有益吗？多数报纸对恐怖分子的意义比恐怖分子本身还大。请谨慎选择信息来源，因为它们常以耸动标题勾起兴趣、牺牲事实。社交媒体用得好是绝妙工具，滥用则极具破坏力，会让人越用越孤立。
广告也常是污染的信息来源，比如高糖不健康食品的广告。糖是人类的全球头号健康威胁，每年致死人数超过海洛因、可卡因和安非他命之和。面对这些产品与广告时，我们要对自己的念头和冲动负责，明白对方诱导你消费并非为你的利益。

keyPoints.phrase: Advertisements are also sources of often polluted information
synonyms: ads are also a polluted source

keyPoints.phrase: take responsibility over our thoughts and impulses

clips.summary: 人类的「操作系统」经数百万年演化，为的是奖励在匮乏、充满威胁的环境中求生存的行为，如今却已危险地过时，是时候升级了：从聪明的猴子进化为有意识的生命。你和我一样是智人、是进化的顶点；最该恐惧的不是残酷事件本身，而是你不愿掌控自己对事件的反应。能否对念头负起全部责任，将决定你乃至整个世界的走向。

keyPoints.phrase: take full responsibility for your thoughts
synonyms: take full ownership of your thoughts
